def atomic(path, data):

**这次卡在 USB 驱动识别摄像头的阶段，摄像头采集还没开始，所以没有预览。** 之前能正常预览的实测仍然有效。

本次日志显示：

1. 板子识别到了 USB 集线器，但没有完成摄像头识别。
2. 等待预览约 30 秒后超时，语音启动流程也随之退出。
3. 你重新插接摄像头后，驱动明确报“控制端点分配失败 `-16`”，意思是资源被判定为占用。

这版构建记录确认只改了无线部分，摄像头驱动和预览代码沿用了上一版。但**代码没改，不代表不同启动时序下不会触发已有问题**。目前重点怀疑 USB 设备槽或端点状态的管理问题，具体根因尚未证实；不能据此说摄像头坏了或你没接好。

我上一条只报了故障，没有解释清楚。下一步需要对照之前成功启动时的 USB 状态，定位占用从哪里产生。
继续对照之前能正常预览的版本，找出原因修好，尽快上板把三图上传、报告播放和恢复跟随测完，保留r22回退，别改其他正常功能。
我会对照可正常预览版本的 USB 驱动和启动记录，定位后只修摄像头启动阻点，尽快上板完成三图上传、报告播放和恢复跟随测试；保留 r22 回退及其他正常功能。

def frozen_pcm_read_completed(command, text):
    """Bind a read completion to exact output ranges if its console echo lost bytes.

    This does not accept PCM contents: the exporter separately validates every
    hex sample, frozen identity and whole-stream CRC. No mutating command can
    use this path, and a prompt/result alone cannot acknowledge a request.
    """
    request = re.fullmatch(r'k7sound echo-diag-dump (mic|reference|residual|zero) ([0-9]+) ([0-9]+)', command)
    if not request:

    kind, first, count = request.group(1), int(request.group(2)), int(request.group(3))
    if not 1 <= count <= 1024 or not 0 <= first < 480000 or first+count > 480000:
        return False
    results = list(re.finditer(r'^ECHO_DIAG_COMMAND result=(-?[0-9]+)$', text, re.M))
    if len(results) != 1 or results[0].group(1) != '0' or not re.search(r'(?:^|\n)nsh>[ \t]+', text[results[0].end():]):
        return False
    headers = re.findall(r'^ECHO_DIAG_PCM kind=(mic|reference|residual|zero) owner=([0-9]+) generation=([0-9]+) instance=([0-9]+) epoch=([0-9]+) offset=([0-9]+) count=([0-9]+) data=', text[:results[0].start()], re.M)
    cursor = first
    identity = None
    for name, owner, generation, instance, epoch, offset, n in headers:
        ids = tuple(map(int, (owner, generation, instance, epoch)))
        n, offset = int(n), int(offset)
        if name != kind or any(x <= 0 for x in ids) or (identity is not None and ids != identity) or offset != cursor or not 1 <= n <= 64 or cursor+n > first+count:

        identity = ids
        cursor += n
    return bool(headers) and cursor == first+count

param(

$script:quiescentCaptureProof=$null
$script:quiescentCaptureLast=$null

function Normalize-Quiescent([string]$Text) {
  return ($Text -replace '\r+\n',"`n").Trim([char[]]"`r`n `0")
}
function Get-QuiescentProofUtc($Value) {
  if ($Value -is [DateTime]) {return $Value.ToUniversalTime()}
  return [DateTimeOffset]::Parse([string]$Value,[Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture).UtcDateTime
}
function Get-QuiescentPromptPattern {
  # Read-Native removes ANSI but not heartbeats before matching. Permit only
  # complete source-format heartbeats after the prompt, never arbitrary text.
  return '(?:^|\n)nsh>[ \t]*(?:(?:\r*\n)?(?:'+(Get-QuiescentRadioHeartbeatPattern)+'|'+(Get-QuiescentRadioAckPattern)+'|VVBOOT alive elapsed_s=\d+ services_ready=1\r*\n))*$'
}
function Get-QuiescentRadioAckPattern {
  # Only the complete healthy two-line ACK observed in the reviewed raw logs.
  # A shared sequence is mandatory; single/partial lines and errors survive.
  return '(?-i:RADIO Wi-Fi RX type=1 id=15 seq=(?<quiescentAckSeq>[0-9]+) len=10\r*\n'+
    'RADIO Wi-Fi cmd=15 seq=\k<quiescentAckSeq> ack=1 status=0 response=0 ret=0\r*\n)'
}
function Get-QuiescentRadioHeartbeatPattern {
  # Exact k7boot/radio snapshot, including the unconfigured offline state.
  # It may immediately follow the prompt in the same serial read. Partial
  # groups and arbitrary errors are not accepted or stripped.
  $ip='(?:none|\d+(?:\.\d+){3})'
  return 'VVBOOT alive elapsed_s=\d+ services_ready=1\r*\n'+
    'WIFI status active=[01] wifi_connected=[01] ip='+$ip+' gateway='+$ip+' result=0\r*\n'+
    'WIFI frame_tx drops=\d+\r*\n'+
    'WIFI netdev rx=\d+ tx=\d+ dropped=\d+\r*\n'+
    'WIFI ARP rx_request=\d+ rx_reply=\d+ tx_request=\d+ tx_reply=\d+ wait_ms=250 retries=5\r*\n'+
    'WIFI AMSDU complete=\d+ subframes=\d+ rejected=\d+\r*\n'+
    'RADIO BLE name=VelaVision K7 connected=[01] handle=\d+ ACL_RX=\d+ ACL_TX_queued=\d+\r*\n'+
    'RADIO BLE history connections=\d+ disconnections=\d+ last_reason=\d+ encrypt_status=0 encrypted=[01]\r*\n'+
    'RADIO ble-status ret=0\r*\n'
}
function Get-QuiescentBody([string]$Reply,[string]$Command) {
  $clean=$Reply -replace '\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]',''
  if ($clean -match 'TRACK |PHOTO RAM|VOICE MODE applied=') {throw 'Preview/photo activity: not quiescent'}
  # Once per minute VVBOOT emits this exact read-only radio snapshot. It can
  # split a byte-paced command echo. Preserve raw evidence; remove only the
  # complete known-format block, never arbitrary WIFI/RADIO errors or text.
  $clean=$clean -creplace (Get-QuiescentRadioHeartbeatPattern),''
  $clean=$clean -creplace (Get-QuiescentRadioAckPattern),''
  $clean=$clean -replace 'VVBOOT alive elapsed_s=\d+ services_ready=1\r*\n',''
  # RX_MGMT metadata can interrupt a byte-paced echo even with preview stopped.
  # This header is not a success status. Keep all management/link error output;
  # remove only the complete type/id/length observed in the reviewed receipt.
  $clean=$clean -creplace 'RADIO Wi-Fi RX type=2 id=4 seq=[0-9]+ len=70\r*\n',''
  $clean=$clean -replace '\r+\n',"`n"
  $echo=$Command+"`n"
  $at=$clean.IndexOf($echo,[StringComparison]::Ordinal)
  if ($at -lt 0 -or $clean -notmatch '(?:^|\n)nsh>[ \t]*$') {throw 'Incomplete exact echo or final prompt'}
  $tail=$clean.Substring($at+$echo.Length)
  return Normalize-Quiescent $tail.Substring(0,$tail.LastIndexOf('nsh>'))
}
function Get-QuiescentPids([string]$Body) {
  $m=[regex]::Match($Body+"`n",'(?:^|\n)/proc:\n((?: [0-9]+/\n)+) fs/\n')
  if (-not $m.Success) {throw 'Incomplete proc PID section/fs marker'}
  $ids=@([regex]::Matches($m.Groups[1].Value,' ([0-9]+)/\n') | ForEach-Object {[int]$_.Groups[1].Value} | Sort-Object)
  if ($ids.Count -lt 8 -or $ids.Count -gt 64 -or @($ids | Select-Object -Unique).Count -ne $ids.Count) {throw 'Incomplete/duplicate task inventory'}
  return ,$ids

"}

import argparse

def fields(text, prefix):
    lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line.startswith(prefix)]
    if len(lines) != 1:
        raise ValueError('Missing or duplicate status: ' + prefix)
    base = prefix.rsplit(' ', 1)[0]

        raise ValueError('Malformed status: ' + prefix)
    pairs = re.findall(r'([a-z_]+)=(-?\d+)', lines[0])
    if len({k for k, _ in pairs}) != len(pairs):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate status field: ' + prefix)
    return {k: int(v) for k, v in pairs}


READ_ONLY_COMMANDS = {'display': 'k7display status',
                      'capture-service-status': 'k7host capture-service-status',
                      'native-status': 'k7cloud native-status'}


def checked_receipt(receipt, command, owner, state, now):
    request = receipt.get('request', {})
    event = receipt.get('queue_event', {})
    if (receipt.get('status') != 'response_received' or
            request.get('target_owner_pid') != owner or
            request.get('command') != READ_ONLY_COMMANDS[command] or
            event.get('status') != 'sent' or event.get('id') != request.get('id') or
            event.get('command') != request.get('command')):
        raise ValueError('Receipt does not belong to this owner and diagnostic')

            not 0 <= now - state.get('checked_epoch', 0) < 5):
        raise ValueError('UART owner changed or stopped during diagnostic')
    return receipt['output']


def voice_counts(observed):
    """Count complete source-format rounds; reuse attempts are not successes."""
    text = re.sub(rb'\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]', b'', observed).replace(b'\r', b'')
    counts = dict(asr_success_rounds=0, warm_reuse_attempts=0,
                  warm_reuse_rounds=0, asr_failed_rounds=0,
                  native_retry_events=0, native_exit_events=0,
                  radio_rx_faults=0, capture_cleanup_failures=0)
    warm = None
    # The final incomplete line cannot establish either success or failure.
    for line in text.split(b'\n')[:-1]:
        if line == b'NATIVE_ASR stage=1 rc=0 streaming=1':
            warm = None
        reuse = re.fullmatch(rb'PARAFORMER capture_session_reused=([01])', line)
        if reuse:
            warm = reuse[1] == b'1'
            counts['warm_reuse_attempts'] += int(warm)
        result = re.fullmatch(rb'NATIVE_ASR stage=2 rc=(-?\d+) http=(-?\d+)', line)

                counts['warm_reuse_rounds'] += int(warm is True)
            else:
                counts['asr_failed_rounds'] += 1
            warm = None
        counts['native_retry_events'] += int(line.startswith(b'NATIVE_RETRY '))
        counts['native_exit_events'] += int(line.startswith(
            (b'VVALIYUN stage=service_exit ', b'VVALIYUN stage=sequence_exit ')))
        counts['radio_rx_faults'] += int(b'RADIO RX fault' in line)
        closed = re.fullmatch(rb'PARAFORMER capture_session_closed rc=(-?\d+)', line)

            counts['capture_cleanup_failures'] += 1

                'radio_rx_faults', 'capture_cleanup_failures'):

                else:

                    if n['configured'] != 1 or n['running'] != 1 or n['stopping'] != 0:
                        raise ValueError('Native voice service not running')

                if snapshot['capture']['bad'] != prev['capture']['bad']:
                    raise ValueError('USB bad-slot counter increased during soak')
            report['snapshots'].append(snapshot)
            if raw_log.stat().st_size < raw_offset:

    return 0 if report['status'] == 'bounded_preview_voice_soak_passed' else 1

    limit = {'source': 480000, 'mic': 1472000}.get(kind, 0)
    if type(offset) is not int or type(count) is not int or not 0 <= offset < limit or not 1 <= count <= 4096 or offset + count > limit:
        raise ValueError('session-capture-dump requires --kind and bounded --offset/--count')
    return 'k7sound session-capture-dump {} {} {}'.format(kind, offset, count)


def echo_dump_command(kind, offset, count):
    if kind not in ('mic', 'reference', 'residual', 'zero') or type(offset) is not int or type(count) is not int or not 0 <= offset < 480000 or not 1 <= count <= 1024 or offset + count > 480000:
        raise ValueError('echo-dump requires a stream and bounded sample offset/count')
    return 'k7sound echo-diag-dump {} {} {}'.format(kind, offset, count)


def echo_tail_dump_command(offset, count):
    if type(offset) is not int or type(count) is not int or not 0 <= offset < 21440 or not 1 <= count <= 1024 or offset + count > 21440:
        raise ValueError('echo-tail-dump requires bounded RAW sample offset/count')

def echo_anchor_command(offset, count):
    if type(offset) is not int or type(count) is not int or not 0 <= offset < 4096 or not 1 <= count <= 32 or offset + count > 4096:

    return 'k7sound echo-diag-anchors {} {}'.format(offset, count)


def frozen_pcm_read_completed(command, text):
    """Bind a read completion to exact output ranges if its console echo lost bytes.

    This does not accept PCM contents: the exporter separately validates every
    hex sample, frozen identity and whole-stream CRC. No mutating command can
    use this path, and a prompt/result alone cannot acknowledge a request.
    """
    request = re.fullmatch(r'k7sound echo-diag-dump (mic|reference|residual|zero) ([0-9]+) ([0-9]+)', command)
    if not request:
        return False
    kind, first, count = request.group(1), int(request.group(2)), int(request.group(3))
    if not 1 <= count <= 1024 or not 0 <= first < 480000 or first+count > 480000:
        return False
    results = list(re.finditer(r'^ECHO_DIAG_COMMAND result=(-?[0-9]+)$', text, re.M))
    if len(results) != 1 or results[0].group(1) != '0' or not re.search(r'(?:^|\n)nsh>[ \t]+', text[results[0].end():]):
        return False
    headers = re.findall(r'^ECHO_DIAG_PCM kind=(mic|reference|residual|zero) owner=([0-9]+) generation=([0-9]+) instance=([0-9]+) epoch=([0-9]+) offset=([0-9]+) count=([0-9]+) data=', text[:results[0].start()], re.M)
    cursor = first
    identity = None
    for name, owner, generation, instance, epoch, offset, n in headers:
        ids = tuple(map(int, (owner, generation, instance, epoch)))
        n, offset = int(n), int(offset)
        if name != kind or any(x <= 0 for x in ids) or (identity is not None and ids != identity) or offset != cursor or not 1 <= n <= 64 or cursor+n > first+count:
            return False
        identity = ids
        cursor += n
    return bool(headers) and cursor == first+count

# New Alexa feature enables natural, multiparty interactions

## In Conversation Mode, Alexa detects device-directed speech without the need for the wake word.

By the Alexa AI team

November 18, 2021

3 min read

Alexa’s Conversation Mode — which we announced last year and are launching today — represents a major milestone in voice AI. Conversation Mode will let Echo Show 8 and Echo Show 10 customers interact with Alexa more naturally, without the need to repeat the wake word.

Using a combination of visual and acoustic cues, the feature’s AI will recognize when customer speech is directed at the device and whether a reply is expected. A customer can invoke Conversation Mode by saying, “Alexa, turn on Conversation Mode” and exit by saying, “Turn off Conversation Mode”. Alternatively, Alexa will exit the mode if there is no interaction for a short period of time.

Image: Conversation Mode.png

Conversation Mode measures visual device directedness by estimating the head orientation of each person in the device’s field of view.

Conversation Mode enables one or more customers to engage with Alexa simultaneously. This makes detecting device directedness even harder, since a question like ‘How about a comedy?’ could be directed at Alexa or at another customer.

The feature also needs to have a low latency, to accurately detect the start of a device-directed utterance; otherwise, Alexa might not capture the full utterance. This is easier in wake-word-based interactions, as the detection of the wake word provides a defined starting point for processing an utterance.

Enabling wake-word-free interactions for Conversation Mode required innovations in several areas, including visual device directedness detection, audio-based voice activity detection, and audiovisual feature fusion.

L16: > Abstract:Follow-up conversations with virtual assistants (VAs) enable a user to seamlessly interact with a VA without the need to repeatedly invoke it using a keyword (after the first query). L17: To this end, we explore the notion of Large Language Models (LLMs) and model the first query when making inference about the follow-ups (based on the ASR-decoded text), via prompting of a pretrained LLM, or by adapting a binary classifier on top of the LLM. L18: We show on the real-world dataset of follow-up conversations that this approach yields large gains (20-40% reduction in false alarms at 10% fixed false rejects) due to the joint modeling of the previous speech context and ASR uncertainty, compared to when follow-ups are modeled alone.

L4: ### Device-directed Utterance Detection
L5: ##### Sri Harish Mallidi, Roland Maas, Kyle Goehner, Ariya Rastrow, Spyros Matsoukas, Björn Hoffmeister
L6: In this work, we propose a classifier for distinguishing device-directed queries from background speech in the context of interactions with voice assistants. Applications include rejection of false wake-ups or unintended interactions as well as enabling wake-word free follow-up queries. Consider the example interaction: "Computer, play music", "Computer, reduce the volume". In this interaction, the user needs to repeat the wake-word (Computer) for the second query.
L7: To allow for more natural interactions, the device could immediately re-enter listening state after the first query (without wake-word repetition) and accept or reject a potential follow-up as device-directed or background speech. The proposed model consists of two long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks trained on acoustic features and automatic speech recognition (ASR) 1-best hypotheses, respectively.
L8: A feed-forward deep neural network (DNN) is then trained to combine the acoustic and 1-best embeddings, derived from the LSTMs, with features from the ASR decoder. Experimental results show that ASR decoder, acoustic embeddings and 1-best embeddings yield an equal-error-rate (EER) of 9.3%, 10.9% and 20.1%, respectively. Combination of the features resulted in a 44% relative improvement and a final EER of 5.2%.

L16: > Abstract:When interacting with smart devices such as mobile phones or wearables, the user typically invokes a virtual assistant (VA) by saying a keyword or by pressing a button on the device. However, in many cases, the VA can accidentally be invoked by the keyword-like speech or accidental button press, which may have implications on user experience and privacy.
L17: To this end, we propose an acoustic false-trigger-mitigation (FTM) approach for on-device device-directed speech detection that simultaneously handles the voice-trigger and touch-based invocation. To facilitate the model deployment on-device, we introduce a new streaming decision layer, derived using the notion of temporal convolutional networks (TCN) [1], known for their computational efficiency.
L18: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first approach that can detect device-directed speech from more than one invocation type in a streaming fashion.
L19: We compare this approach with streaming alternatives based on vanilla Average layer, and canonical LSTMs, and show: (i) that all the models show only a small degradation in accuracy compared with the invocation-specific models, and (ii) that the newly introduced streaming TCN consistently performs better or comparable with the alternatives, while mitigating device undirected speech faster in time, and with (relative) reduction in runtime peak-memory over the LSTM-based approach of 33% vs.
L20: 7%, when compared to a non-streaming counterpart.

L16: > Abstract:Follow-up conversations with virtual assistants (VAs) enable a user to seamlessly interact with a VA without the need to repeatedly invoke it using a keyword (after the first query). Therefore, accurate Device-directed Speech Detection (DDSD) from the follow-up queries is critical for enabling naturalistic user experience.
L17: To this end, we explore the notion of Large Language Models (LLMs) and model the first query when making inference about the follow-ups (based on the ASR-decoded text), via prompting of a pretrained LLM, or by adapting a binary classifier on top of the LLM. In doing so, we also exploit the ASR uncertainty when designing the LLM prompts.
L18: We show on the real-world dataset of follow-up conversations that this approach yields large gains (20-40% reduction in false alarms at 10% fixed false rejects) due to the joint modeling of the previous speech context and ASR uncertainty, compared to when follow-ups are modeled alone.
